title: Quantile Treatment Effects with Outcome-Dependent Loss and Fixed-Size Chart Recovery
banked_reason: D0.5.G graded subfield below field floor, paper score ceiling 7.2 below 7.4; estimator formula and all-budget scope remain unresolved.
gap_reasons: graded tier 'subfield' against target 'field' (floor 'field'): under the bar; no bounded fix in scope
paper_score_ceiling 7.2 < 7.4, so the graded tier 'field' is capped at 'subfield'

The all-budget theorems are formally imprecise because \(\mathcal M_n\) is defined using sequence-level conditions while the displayed supremum is written over a single \(n\)-section with an apparently law-dependent \(r_n\)
proof_attempt_summary: D0 constructed a Gaussian-binomial local minimax transfer, a one-chart correction, and richness-conditional all-budget bounds, then repaired a uniform-class scope mismatch, density normalization, and pilot/recovery overlap accounting. D0.5 stopped at subfield below the required field floor (score ceiling 7.2 versus 7.4). An independent validity audit found that the feasible estimator still lacks an exact formula and proved bias/L2 bounds, and the all-budget supremum mixes sequence and n-section scope; this archive is not a verified sound theorem or Lean formalization.
tldr: In a balanced randomized cohort with arbitrary outcome-dependent initial loss and arm-specific fixed-size chart recovery, critical missingness leaves finite binomial nuisance information beside the Gaussian cohort coordinate. Uniform transfer and local minimaxity are asserted over an explicitly fixed nonempty family \(\mathfrak R\) with common critical-scaling and pool-growth moduli; arbitrary pointwise critical arrays support only the pointwise expansion. On that family the data-only correction attains the exact Gaussian--binomial local minimax absolute risk, and the feasible one-chart quarter--three-quarter correction attains \(L_\sigma(b/4)\), strictly improving on empirical correction. Across all admitted budgets, the weighted empirical-quantile estimator and honest CDF-inversion interval have upper order \(r_n\); under the separately disclosed smooth richness premise, explicit two-point witnesses give matching minimax-risk and interval-diameter lower orders.
gap: Existing causal double-sampling quantile theory assumes a second-stage sampling probability bounded away from zero, so its recovered-data term is Gaussian and bootstrap calibration has an increasing nuisance sample. Classical Bernoulli minimax theory covers the finite threshold count but not its sharp transfer to a causal quantile experiment.
fill: The project characterizes and attains the Gaussian--binomial local minimax value, derives the exact one-chart correction and empirical risk gap, proves the empirical law cannot be learned, and supports the focal transfer with a matched all-budget risk rate and a fully specified finite-sample CDF-inversion interval.
